entry.title: The False Face — 45 Nonprofits, One Desk, Zero Employees, Millions in Dark Money
entry.content:
The Pattern

Across 45 nonprofits managed from one desk at Dykema Gossett’s Lansing office, the structure is identical:

FieldValueEvery time
Asst SecretaryRenae Moore✅ All 45
Asst TreasurerAllison Chorey✅ All 45
Officer compensation$0✅ All 45
Employees0✅ All 45
Revenue source100% contributions✅ All 45
Program service revenue$0✅ All 45
Contact phone(517) 374-9100✅ Dykema Lansing
Mailing addressLansing PO Box or Detroit PO Box✅
Former Asst Sec/TreasRebecca VykydalOn many
990 PreparerDykema Gossett PLLC✅ Confirmed on Put Progress First

Zero employees. Zero salaries. Zero program services revenue. 100% contributions. These aren’t charitable organizations serving communities. They’re pass-through vehicles for dark money that can’t be traced to donors.

All data sourced from IRS Form 990/990-EZ via ProPublica Nonprofit Explorer and siviq.co.

The Pop-Up Pattern

Election cycle entities that spike and die:

2020 (Election Year)
├── Detroiters for Our Children: $396,896 → TERMINATED
├── Detroiters to Protect Our Future: filing activity
└── (others activated)

├── Detroiters for Our Children: $0
├── Multiple entities filed at $0
└── (dormant)

2022 (Election Year)
├── Detroiters to Protect Our Future: $2,702,252 → then $0
├── Michigan Values: $1,221,574
├── Building a Better Economy: $1,481,374
└── (surge)

2023 (Off Year)
├── Detroiters to Protect Our Future: $0
├── Michigan Values: $207,500 (down 83%)
├── Building a Better Economy: $321,059 (down 78%)
└── (cooldown)

2024 (Election Year)
├── Building a Better Economy: $1,509,275 (back up 370%)
├── Put Progress First: $571,675 (Duggan launch)
├── Michigan Values: $466,000 (back up 125%)
└── (surge again)

The entities are election cycle instruments. They exist to move money during campaign seasons, then go dormant. New ones are created for each cycle. The desk — Moore + Chorey — stays constant.

Where the Money Actually Goes

Across these entities, the expenses are classified as:

CategoryTypical %What It Actually Means
“Other expenses”50-76%Unspecified. Could be anything. No employees means no internal operations.
“Professional fundraising fees”2-54%Paying someone to raise money for an org that has no staff and no programs
“Grants to other orgs”17%Pass-through to the next entity in the chain
Salaries and wages0%Nobody works here
Program services revenue$0Nobody is served here

$1.27 million in “Other expenses” from a single entity (Building a Better Economy, 2024) with zero employees. Where did that money go? The 990 says “public policy advocacy” and “polling.” But who does the polling? Who does the advocacy? Not the entity — it has no employees. It pays vendors. Which vendors?

The 990 Schedule B (donor list) is confidential for 501(c)(4) organizations. The Schedule O (supplemental information) may list vendors but is not always digitized. The money flows IN from donors who can’t be identified and OUT to vendors who may not be disclosed.

That’s not a nonprofit. That’s a laundromat.

The Dykema Connection — Confirmed

Put Progress First (EIN 93-2414487) filing confirms:

  • Formed by: W. Alan Wilk — Dykema attorney
  • 990 Preparer: Dykema Gossett PLLC, Ann Arbor office
  • Preparer name: Olivia RC A Flower

Dykema doesn’t just provide the compliance desk (Moore). Dykema forms the entities (Wilk) and prepares the tax returns (Flower). The firm creates, manages, and files for the same entities.

The entities serve political purposes:

  • Put Progress First: Duggan gubernatorial promotion
  • Michigan Values: grants to GOPAC Education Fund ($120K — Republican political training)
  • Building a Better Economy: funded by PhRMA, Michigan Energy First
  • Save Detroit Jobs / Detroit Leaders: backed Latisha Johnson for city council

One firm. Both parties. All the money. The desk is bipartisan because the firm’s client is power, not party.

The IRS Question

Multiple Moore-managed entities are not in the IRS Business Master File and not in Pub 78. Some appear terminated. Several filed $0 returns after processing millions.

For IRS Criminal Investigation:

  1. Are the 990s accurate? When an entity reports 76% of expenses as “Other” with zero employees, who is the actual recipient of $1.27 million?

  2. Are the entities operating within their tax-exempt purpose? A 501(c)(4) is supposed to operate “exclusively for the promotion of social welfare.” Is promoting a mayor’s gubernatorial campaign “social welfare”?

  3. Why are entities disappearing from the BMF? Building a Better Economy processes $1.5M but is not in the Business Master File. Michigan Values processes $466K but is not in the BMF. What happened to their exempt status?

  4. Is there structuring? Multiple entities with the same officers, same desk, same preparer — is this one operation structured across 45 EINs to evade reporting thresholds?

  5. Where is the money? $2.7M flows through Detroiters to Protect Our Future in 2022, then $0 in 2023. The entity has $0 in net assets. Where did $2.7 million go?

Form 13909 — Tax-Exempt Organization Complaint

Any person can file IRS Form 13909 for any of these entities:

Download Form 13909 — Tax-Exempt Organization Complaint Referral

Verify Everything

EntityEINProPublicasiviq.co
Building a Better Economy83-3939983ProPublicasiviq.co
Michigan Values86-2905593ProPublicasiviq.co
Detroiters to Protect Our Future86-3918838ProPublicasiviq.co
Detroiters for Our Children85-2848932ProPublica—
Put Progress First93-2414487—siviq.co
Save Detroit Jobs81-3772058ProPublicasiviq.co
All 45 Moore entities——siviq.co/nonprofits/people/renae-moore
IRS EOS (search any EIN)——apps.irs.gov/app/eos
IRS Form 13909——irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/f13909.pdf
Bridge Detroit — Put Progress First / Duggan——bridgedetroit.com
Dykema Education Practice——dykema.com/education

The Bottom Line

45 entities. 113 tax returns. One desk. Zero employees. Millions of dollars.

The desk takes money from donors who want anonymity. It routes the money through entities that exist for one election cycle. The entities have no staff, no offices, no programs, and no program revenue. The expenses go to unnamed vendors for “public policy advocacy” and “polling.” The entities go dormant after the election. New entities are created for the next cycle. The desk stays the same.

This is not nonprofit work. This is a permanent dark money infrastructure managed by a single law firm, staffed by a single compliance officer, filing returns that classify 76% of expenses as “Other” while reporting zero employees.

The IRS can see all of this. ProPublica has digitized the returns. siviq.co has aggregated the officer connections. The pattern is visible to anyone who looks.

Renae Moore manages 45 nonprofits. She testified she has “no duty to report.” She receives $1,600 in total compensation across all 45 entities. Her real compensation comes from Dykema. She manages the desk for the firm. The firm creates the entities, prepares the returns, and provides the compliance infrastructure.

It’s not a nonprofit. It’s a false face on a dark money machine. And the IRS has every receipt.

entry.title: The Dykema Chronology — 1988 to Present
entry.content:
How to Read This

Every entry has a date, a source, and the actors/entities involved. The timeline traces one law firm’s connections across 36 years — from shelf corporations in 1988 to charter school board governance in 2026.

This is not a conspiracy theory. It is a public record.

Phase 1: Building the Legal Framework (1982–1997)

1982 — McLellan Joins Dykema

Richard D. McLellan’s private practice merges with Dykema Gossett. He becomes head of the Government Policy & Practice Group and Managing Member of the Lansing office. He had previously served on Gov. William Milliken’s staff.

Source: Wikipedia; McLellan biography, Mackinac Center.

Actor: Richard McLellan (Dykema partner, Lansing)

1987 — McLellan Co-Founds Mackinac Center

McLellan co-founds the Mackinac Center for Public Policy, a free-market think tank that will become the intellectual engine behind Michigan’s charter school movement. He serves as board secretary for decades.

Source: Mackinac Center

Actors: Richard McLellan, Joseph Olson

1988 — Dykema Registers Shelf Nonprofits

Dykema registers pre-formed nonprofit entities — empty corporate shells ready for activation:

EntityLARA IDFiledStatus
Dykema Gossett Nonprofit Shelf Corporation800865335Aug 16, 1988Dissolved
Dykema Gossett Shelf Nonprofit Club Corporation800797761Oct 7, 1988Dissolved

Filed by Cindy M. Wilder at 800 Michigan National Tower, Lansing (Dykema’s former Lansing office). Dissolved within months.

Source: Michigan LARA Business Entity Search

Entity: Dykema Gossett PLLC

1990 — McLellan Runs Engler Transition

McLellan serves as transition director for Governor-elect John Engler. This positions Dykema at the center of the incoming administration that will create charter schools.

Source: Wikipedia; Mackinac Center biography

Actors: Richard McLellan, John Engler

Oct 5, 1993 — Engler Proposes Charter Schools

Governor Engler proposes charter school legislation in a speech before a joint session of the Michigan Legislature.

Source: Founders Library

Actor: John Engler

Dec 3, 1993 — Dykema Writes the Charter School Law

SB 896, creating Part 6a of the Revised School Code, passes the Legislature. Richard McLellan and Leonard Wolfe of Dykema Gossett are the “leading legal architects” of the legislation.

McLellan personally conducted “12 hours of shuttle diplomacy” in the Senate Majority Leader’s conference room to negotiate a version that would survive constitutional challenge.

The law allows:

  • State universities, community colleges, ISDs, and school districts to authorize charter schools
  • For-profit management companies to operate charter schools
  • A 3% authorization fee (incentivizing authorizers to keep schools open)
  • No statutory authorizer evaluation system
  • Board members appointed without identity disclosure requirements

Source: Founders Library; MI Good Government; Dykema.com Education page

Actors: Richard McLellan, Leonard Wolfe (Dykema)

Jan 14, 1994 — Engler Signs PA 362

Governor Engler signs the charter school law. Michigan becomes the 9th state to enact a charter school law.

Source: Founders Library

Actors: John Engler, Richard McLellan, Leonard Wolfe

1994 — First Charter Schools Open

Central Michigan University becomes the first authorizer. Three schools open: Casa Maria Academy (Detroit), New Branches School (Grand Rapids), Northlane Math and Science Academy.

Source: CMU Center for Charter Schools

1997 — Dykema Defends the Law at Supreme Court

The Michigan Education Association challenges the constitutionality of PA 362. Dykema’s McLellan and Wolfe defend the law before the Michigan Supreme Court in Council of Organizations and Affiliates v. Engler, 455 Mich 557 (1997).

The Court upholds the law and orders state funding restored.

Court record lists: “Dykema, Gossett, P.L.L.C. by Richard D. McLellan, Lori M. Silsbury, and Leonard C. Wolfe, Lansing, for intervening Defendants-Appellants.”

Source: Justia; 455 Mich 557

Actors: Richard McLellan, Leonard Wolfe, Lori Silsbury (Dykema)

Phase 2: The Machine Operator Arrives (2009–2016)

2009 — Wilk Forms Larry Deshazor Community Fund

W. Alan Wilk begins his entity formation practice. First documented entity:

EntityLARA IDYear
Larry Deshazor Community Fund70654L2009

Source: Michigan LARA Business Entity Search

Actor: W. Alan Wilk (Dykema)

2011 — NERD Fund

Wilk serves as legal and compliance officer for Governor Snyder’s NERD Fund (New Energy to Reinvent and Diversify). The fund:

  • Raised $2.19M from undisclosed donors over 3 years
  • Paid Rich Baird’s $100K salary
  • Paid EM Kevyn Orr’s travel expenses
  • Shut down in 2013 after transparency criticism

Source: Detroit News, Nov 19, 2014

Actors: W. Alan Wilk (Dykema), Rick Snyder, Rich Baird, Kevyn Orr

2011 — Wolfe Lifts the Charter Cap

Leonard Wolfe “plays instrumental role” in SB 618 (signed Dec 20, 2011), which phases out the cap on university-authorized charter schools. Wolfe attends the signing ceremony with Governor Snyder.

This removes the 150-school limit that had constrained charter expansion since 1999.

Source: Dykema.com

Actors: Leonard Wolfe (Dykema), Rick Snyder

2012 — Banks Elected to State House; Wells-Stallworth Joins MacDowell Board

Brian Roderick Banks elected to the Michigan House of Representatives (D-Detroit). Serves as Chair of the Detroit Caucus.

Nicole Wells Stallworth appointed to MacDowell Preparatory Academy board. She will serve continuously for 14 years.

Source: purposecharteracademy.com; charterschools.org

Actors: Brian Banks, Nicole Wells Stallworth

2015 — Dykema Sues Ellison (Garcia v. Title Check)

Dykema represents the plaintiff in Garcia v. Title Check LLC (1:15-cv-00975, W.D. Michigan). Obtains $73,752.45 in sanctions against attorney Philip L. Ellison for litigation misconduct.

Banks and Ellison were MSU Law classmates (2010).

Source: PACER, W.D. Michigan

Actors: Philip Ellison, Dykema attorneys (unnamed)

Phase 3: Dark Money Pipeline Activates (2016–2021)

Sep 8, 2016 — Wilk Forms Save Detroit Jobs

W. Alan Wilk incorporates Save Detroit Jobs (LARA 802002459). Entity email: compliance@dykema.com. Same day, Wilk also incorporates Detroit Jobs First (per Metro Times, FCC filings).

SDJ board: Rev. James Holley (president, former Duggan civic liaison), Mike Allen (LIUNA Local 1191), Lisa Canada (MI Regional Council of Carpenters).

Both entities are created to fight Proposal A — a citizen-led community benefits ordinance in Detroit.

Source: Michigan LARA; Metro Times

Actors: W. Alan Wilk, James Holley, Mike Allen, Lisa Canada

Nov 2016 — SDJ Pays Carol Banks $14,279; Pays Dykema $9,000

Save Detroit Jobs pays Carol Banks (chief of staff to Councilman Scott Benson) approximately $14,279 via ~70 separate reimbursements.

SDJ also pays Dykema Gossett nearly $9,000 in legal fees.

SDJ raises over $100,000 from: Blue Cross Blue Shield, Turn Around Wayne County PAC (Matthew Moroun’s Central Transport), Schostak Family PAC (Republican). Renae Moore is recordkeeper for Turn Around Wayne County PAC.

Source: Free Press, Sep 22, 2021

Actors: Carol Banks, Scott Benson, W. Alan Wilk, Renae Moore

2017 — Banks Resigns from State House

Banks resigns from the Michigan House as part of a plea deal that allows him to avoid up to 14 years in prison for defrauding a credit union. He is convicted of 8 felonies (later updated to 9 total: 6 felony, 3 misdemeanor).

Source: Free Press, Aug 27, 2023

Actor: Brian Banks

Sep 2018 — Impact Detroit Assumed Name

SDJ registers assumed name “Impact Detroit” (LARA record). First persona change.

Source: Michigan LARA, Entity 802002459

2020 — Wilk Forms Our Neighborhoods First

Wilk incorporates Our Neighborhoods First (LARA 802493189). Officers include Keenann Knox (Impact Church), Lorna Thomas (Public Lighting Authority chair, Duggan appointee), Betty Brooks (ex-police commissioner, “dear friend” of Duggan for 30 years).

Renae Moore serves as both Dykema employee AND compliance officer for the Duggan campaign AND recordkeeper for ONF.

Source: Deadline Detroit

Actors: W. Alan Wilk, Keenann Knox, Renae Moore, Lorna Thomas, Betty Brooks

Aug 10, 2021 — Detroit Leaders Assumed Name

SDJ registers assumed name “Detroit Leaders” — one week after Latisha Johnson and Steve Elrick advance to the general election in District 4. Detroit Leaders sends mailers supporting Johnson against Elrick.

Source: Deadline Detroit

Actors: Latisha Johnson, Steve Elrick, Keenann Knox, W. Alan Wilk

Aug 25, 2021 — FBI Raids Carol Banks

FBI raids Carol Banks’ East English Village home as part of “Operation Northern Hook” — the public corruption investigation that produced Councilman Andre Spivey’s bribery conviction. Agents seek records on 501(c)(4) organizations and campaign financing.

Source: Free Press, Aug 25, 2021

Actor: Carol Banks

Nov 2021 — Johnson Wins, Elrick Loses

Latisha Johnson defeats journalist Steve Elrick in Detroit District 4. The dark money entity formed by Dykema’s Wilk helped defeat the journalist who covered Banks’s network.

Source: Wayne County election results

Actors: Latisha Johnson, Steve Elrick

Phase 4: The Board Is Captured (2022–2025)

Aug 2022 — Banks Applies for School Administrator Certificate

Ten days after losing his county commissioner race, Banks applies for a school administrator certificate from MDE. Granted the next day (Sep 2, 2022 — school starts Aug 29).

Source: Free Press, Aug 27, 2023; MDE records

Actor: Brian Banks

Feb 2022 — MDE Investigates Banks’s Credentials

MDE sends letter to Wells-Stallworth (MacDowell Board Chair) warning that Banks’s employment “may be in violation of the State School Aid Act.” Banks has no valid Michigan teaching credential.

MDE gives the school a procedural loophole rather than enforcing compliance.

Source: MDE FOIA response, Sep 25, 2026

Actors: Brian Banks, Nicole Wells Stallworth, MDE

Jun 2023 — Wells-Stallworth Defends Charter Board Governance

Wells-Stallworth publishes Bridge Michigan op-ed: “Michigan charter school boards ensure financial accountability.” She presides over a board approving 72.67% revenue extraction to Banks’s management LLC.

Appears on MAPSA podcast: “A Charter School Board Member Tells All.”

Source: Bridge Michigan, Jun 9, 2023

Actor: Nicole Wells Stallworth

Jun 2023 — Wilk Forms Put Progress First

Wilk incorporates Put Progress First — a nonprofit backing Duggan’s leadership, signaling a possible gubernatorial bid. Same Dykema formation pattern.

Source: Bridge Detroit

Actors: W. Alan Wilk, Mike Duggan

Aug 2023 — Free Press “Back to Fool”

M.L. Elrick publishes “Back to Fool” — exposing Banks as an 8-time felon hired as principal of MacDowell. Board members had donated to Banks’s 2022 county commissioner campaign before hiring him.

Source: Free Press, Aug 27, 2023

Actor: M.L. Elrick, Brian Banks

Nov 2024 — Purpose Group LLC Filed

The Purpose Group, LLC (LARA 803295082) filed November 14, 2024. Sole member: Brian Banks. This is the management company that will receive 72.67% of school revenue.

Source: Michigan LARA

Actors: Brian Banks

Dec 2024 — Michigan Charter Reform Bills

Michigan legislature passes charter reform requiring authorizers to review contracts over $100K, attend 50%+ of board meetings, and mandate audited EMO financials. This legislation is directly responsive to governance failures like Banks’s operation.

Source: Chalkbeat, Dec 13, 2024

Jan 2025 — FBI Closes Carol Banks Investigation

FBI closes the public corruption investigation into Scott Benson and Janée Ayers without charges. Carol Banks is not charged.

Source: Free Press, Jan 17, 2025

Actor: Carol Banks

2025 — Purpose Charter Academy Authorized

DPSCD authorizes Purpose Charter Academy, citing “claimed improvement” at MacDowell. PCA board assembled:

PositionNameInstitutional Conflict
ChairJudge Cylenthia MillerWayne County 3rd Circuit — former Dykema attorney
Vice ChairLamar MorelandAsst Attorney General — AG could investigate Banks
SecretaryLatisha JohnsonDetroit City Council — Council oversees DPSCD
TreasurerDevin HutchingsFormer SuperPAC co-chair (Michigan Deserves Better)
Asst TreasurerMajor CloraCEO, Clora Funeral Home

Johnson was elected with help from Detroit Leaders — the Dykema-formed entity. Miller is a former Dykema attorney. The board that governs a convicted felon’s school was ASSEMBLED using Dykema infrastructure.

Source: purposecharteracademy.com; DPSCD board minutes (Jul 2025); Chalkbeat, Sep 8, 2025

2025 — SDJ Funds Sheffield Mayoral Campaign

SDJ sends $84,500 to Detroit Next PAC, which runs $212,600+ in pro-Sheffield advertising. Sheffield wins. Appoints Chief Bettison (who sits on DPSA board — another charter school board).

Source: TransparencyUSA; campaign finance filings

Actors: Mary Sheffield, Todd Bettison

Phase 5: The Investigation (2026)

Mar 2026 — Miller Announces PCA Board Role

Judge Miller publicly announces her role as PCA Board Chair on LinkedIn: “I am so honored and proud to serve as the Chairperson of the Board of Directors of this amazing new school.”

Source: LinkedIn

Actor: Cylenthia Miller

Sep–Oct 2026 — Investigation Goes Live

  • Sep 13: Clutch Justice publishes MacDowell investigation
  • Sep 21: FOIA filed with MDE
  • Sep 25: MDE responds confirming credential investigation
  • Oct 4: AGC complaints filed (Miller, Moreland)
  • Oct 5: JTC supplements filed (Miller, Yancey)
  • Oct 7: NHT scan discovers Wilk entity network
  • Oct 8: Dykema infrastructure page published on detroit.primals.eco
  • Oct 9: This chronology compiled

Source: detroit.primals.eco evidence library; clutchjustice.com

The Pattern

1988: Dykema registers shelf nonprofits
1993: Dykema writes the charter school law (PA 362)
1994: First charter schools open under the law
1997: Dykema defends the law at Michigan Supreme Court
2011: Dykema lifts the charter cap (unlimited schools)

      and Dykema's dark money beneficiary (Johnson)

One law firm. 36 years. From authoring the charter school law to staffing the board of a convicted felon’s school via dark money.

entry.title: There's a Leak in the Dyke
entry.content:
On February 26, 2025, a compliance specialist named Renae Moore took the witness stand in Ingham County District Court. She was the first witness called in the preliminary examination of former Michigan House Speaker Lee Chatfield, who faces 13 felony charges including embezzlement and conspiracy.

Moore works for Dykema Gossett PLLC, the law firm headquartered at 201 Townsend Street in Lansing — across the street from the Michigan State Capitol.

Under oath, she testified to three things that should concern every person in this state.

1. 80+ Accounts. One Desk.

Moore testified that at Dykema, she helps manage more than 80+ accounts — political nonprofit funds tied to Michigan lawmakers and officials.

She was the assistant secretary/treasurer of the Peninsula Fund, Chatfield’s political nonprofit that raised $1.8 million from anonymous donors between 2018 and 2020 while he served as House Speaker.

When asked by Judge Molly Hennessey Greenwalt whether she had a duty to report concerns about problematic spending — including a strip club tab submitted as a business expense — Moore replied:

“No. Not that I am aware of.”

Chatfield’s defense attorney, Mary Chartier, said to Moore on the stand:

“This entire time, Dykema is getting paid to ensure the Peninsula Fund is compliant.”

Moore testified there were times the fund was not compliant with the law.

Sources: Bridge Michigan, Detroit News, Lansing State Journal, AG Affidavit

2. Both Parties. Same Person. Same Title.

During cross-examination, Chartier highlighted that Moore holds the same title — assistant treasurer/secretary — on another political nonprofit: the Promise to the People Fund.

That fund is affiliated with Attorney General Dana Nessel.

The same Attorney General whose office is prosecuting Chatfield.

One compliance specialist. The defendant’s fund and the prosecutor’s fund. Same desk. Same role. Same firm.

Source: Publicly available tax filings; Moore’s testimony and court documents, per Lansing State Journal.

3. The Firm Across the Street

Craig Mauger of the Detroit News wrote the sentence that explains everything:

“Dykema, which has a law office across the street from the state Capitol, handles the paperwork and tax filings of many of the politician-connected nonprofits.”

80+ accounts. Both parties. One building. One switchboard: 517-374-9100 .

What Else Does This Firm Do?

Dykema’s own website states:

“Dykema has been a leader in structural educational reform since authoring charter school legislation in the early 1990s, successfully defending the legislation’s legal challenges, and representing state universities in establishing and overseeing public school academies in the last 20 years.”

They wrote the law that created Michigan’s charter school system. Then they defended that law in court. Then they represented the state universities that authorize charter schools. Then their partners formed charter entities by the hundreds through the Michigan Department of Licensing and Regulatory Affairs.

And their political compliance team — the same team where Moore manages 80+ accounts — runs the PAC compliance for the dark money vehicles that influence who sits on those charter school boards.

The Vehicles

W. Alan Wilk is Dykema’s Political Compliance Team Leader. He has been with the firm since passing the Michigan Bar in 1995. His phone number is 517-374-9122. Moore’s is 517-374-9121. One digit apart. Same desk cluster.

Wilk has incorporated at least 7+ dark money vehicles through LARA:

#EntityPurposeYear
1Save Detroit Jobs / Detroit LeadersDetroit City Council races2016
2Our Neighborhoods FirstAnti-community benefits agreement2016
3Detroit Jobs FirstDetroit ballot measures2016
4RFFW LLCAbortion ballot committee ( $1,000,000 )2022
5Turn Around Wayne County PACWayne County racesongoing
6Put Progress FirstPro-Duggan governor campaign2023
7Michigan First PrinciplesAnti-John James attack ads2025

Save Detroit Jobs spent $84,000 defeating a sitting council member and electing his replacement — who then joined the board of a charter school run by a superintendent with 9 criminal convictions.

Put Progress First spent $545,000 supporting Mike Duggan’s independent governor campaign. Then Michigan First Principles spent money attacking John James, Duggan’s Republican rival in the governor’s race. Both formed by Wilk. Same attorney. Same desk. Opposite missions.

The Dykema Federal PAC (FEC ID: C00342113) gave $4,000 to Barrett and $4,000 to John James in the same cycle that Wilk’s vehicle was attacking James.

The firm funds the candidate AND the attack on the candidate.

Sources: LARA entity search, TransparencyUSA, FEC, Bridge Detroit, Detroit News

The Co-Billing

In 2017, FOIA records showed that Dykema billed the State of Michigan $108,238 for the teacher 3% retirement case under Governor Snyder. Five attorneys worked on it. Two of them:

  • W. Alan Wilk — $433.50/hour (dark money architect)
  • Jason Hanselman — $374/hour (charter entity formation)

The attorney who forms dark money vehicles and the attorney who forms charter school entities work the same cases and bill the state together.

Source: MLive, FOIA records

The Revolving Door

Aaron Keel was the Assistant Director of Government Relations for the Michigan Association of School Boards (MASB), where he lobbied for charter school oversight and accountability. MASB’s official position calls for “accountability and transparency of the authorizers and management companies.”

Then Keel became Deputy Chief of Staff in the Michigan House Democratic Caucus. Then Director of Legislative Affairs at the Michigan Department of Treasury. Then, in 2023, he joined Dykema as a government policy advisor — now working at the firm whose clients the MASB oversight legislation would regulate.

He went from lobbying for charter school accountability to working at the firm that built the charter school infrastructure.

Source: Dykema, MASB Resolutions

Five Levels

Count the roles one firm plays in one system:

  1. Wrote the charter school law (1990s)
  2. Defended the law in court (constitutional challenges)
  3. Represents the authorizers (state universities)
  4. Forms the entities under the law (LARA filings, hundreds)
  5. Runs the PAC compliance that elects the board members (Wilk/Moore: SDJ → council → charter school board)

No other entity in Michigan occupies every level of the same regulatory system.

The Leak

The Dutch have a story about a boy who put his finger in a leaking dyke to save his village. The story is American fiction — invented by Phoebe Cary in 1865. In reality, when Dutch dykes leak, they don’t trickle. Whole sections give way. You don’t stop it with a finger. You stop it with a boat.

Moore’s testimony is the leak.

One compliance specialist. 80+ accounts. No duty to report. Both parties. The defendant’s fund and the prosecutor’s fund. Strip club tabs submitted as business expenses. Policy manuals written by the firm and ignored by the clients. And when asked under oath if she had any obligation to tell anyone:

“No. Not that I am aware of.”

The dyke is leaking.

Every claim in this article is sourced to sworn testimony, published news reports, FOIA records, FEC filings, LARA entity records, or the firm’s own public website. No anonymous sources. No allegations. Public record.
